requirement: Expose SYCL device-link concurrency to Nix's configured build-core budget and retain bounded CUTLASS template diagnostics. This is configurable build behavior, not an established runtime or successful-build performance optimization.

upstream_coverage.selected_source: CMakeLists.txt hardcodes -fsycl-max-parallel-link-jobs=16 and -ftemplate-backtrace-limit=0. It has no equivalent CMake cache-variable controls.
upstream_coverage.newer_release_check: The unselected v0.1.17 source 6a1ec18b69b00eaf67a457e0bdd40e72632feaae still hardcodes the same values at CMakeLists.txt lines 303 and 412; it does not supersede the controls.

nix_consumers.behavior: Split libraries apply 0001 then 0005. preConfigure appends -DVLLM_XPU_SYCL_LINK_PARALLELISM=$NIX_BUILD_CORES to cmakeFlagsArray, so the value is expanded by the build shell. cmakeFlags sets VLLM_XPU_CUTLASS_TEMPLATE_BACKTRACE_LIMIT=10.

The attention library uses compileJobs=12. Its preBuild cap runs after configure captures the original device-link budget, so a 24-core build can use 12 concurrent frontends while retaining 24 device-link jobs. --cores 4 gives four for both. This patch alone does not impose a universal four-job or twelve-job device-link cap.
Base/glue and FA2 binding builds do not apply 0005. MAX_JOBS follows NIX_BUILD_CORES for their build scheduling, but the CMake device-link flag remains the upstream hardcoded 16.

minimal_residual: Keep the existing two cache variables and their flag substitutions unchanged. The device-link control is required for the existing configurable split build. The diagnostic-depth control is independently removable only if its existing diagnostic policy is deliberately retired; upstream has not replaced it. No new flags, architecture changes or patches are needed for the selected pair.
evidence_limits: No controlled A/B measurement of peak memory, elapsed compile time or successful-build benefit was performed here or established by docs/fork-delta.md.
The template-backtrace option primarily bounds diagnostic output; it must not be presented as a proven memory optimization for successful compilations.
No runtime GPU performance effect is claimed.
